drug_class: PI3K inhibitor (a type of targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Duvelisib is used to treat certain types of blood cancers, specifically chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), and follicular lymphoma in adults who have already tried at least two other treatments. It helps slow or stop the growth of cancer cells in your blood and lymph nodes.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have certain proteins called PI3K-delta and PI3K-gamma that help them grow and survive. Duvelisib works like a key that blocks these proteins, essentially turning off the signals that tell cancer cells to keep multiplying. By blocking these signals, the medicine helps slow down or stop the cancer from spreading.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea or loose stools, feeling tired or weak, nausea, fever, cough, rash, stomach pain, low blood counts (which can make you more prone to infections or bruising), and swelling in your arms or legs.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious lung problems (pneumonitis), severe diarrhea or colitis (inflammation of the intestines), liver problems, and serious infections including pneumonia. You should not take it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm an unborn baby. Your doctor will monitor you closely with regular blood tests and check-ups. Tell your doctor right away if you develop severe diarrhea, shortness of breath, signs of infection, or yellowing of your skin or eyes.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 25 mg taken by mouth twice a day, every day. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same times each day. Swallow the capsule whole — do not open, crush, or chew it. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is within 6 hours of your next scheduled dose, in which case just skip it and continue your regular schedule.
